summary: Knut A. Jacobsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD from UC Santa Barbara (~1989–1994). He served as a professor at the University of Bergen (1996) and the University of Oslo (~1996–2000).

Knut Kristiansen (1928–1999) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Georg Morgenstierne at the University of Oslo, where he later served as Universitetslektor in modern Indian languages from 1971 to 1998.

Kobun Otogawa was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kodo Sawaki, Gadjin Nagao, and at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and Eihei-ji. He served at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center (1967–1970) and Haiku Zendo (1970–1978).

Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership posts at Komazawa University, including president in 1909, and lectured at the University of Tokyo.
Kodo Kawamura (1933–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies. He completed his master's and doctoral degrees at Komazawa University, where he also served as a professor from around 1968 to 2004.
Kodo Nomura (1882–1963) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and later served as a researcher at Taisho University.

Kodo Sawaki worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Senju-ji and Horyuji Kangakuin under masters including Sotan Oka and Join Saeki, later serving as professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (~1949–1965).
Kodo Yamada (1866–1933) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who taught at both Komazawa University and Keio University.
Kodo Yotsuya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shiro Matsumoto, earned a master's degree at Komazawa University, and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg.
Koen Wellens is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Charles Willemen at Ghent University and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under doctoral supervisor Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst works in Indology, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at KU Leuven (~1979–1999), where he earned a master's degree, and at Banaras Hindu University (~1988–1992).

Kogen Mizuno earned a Doctorate of Letters from the University of Tokyo (1928), specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1959–1962) and served as president of Komazawa University (1976).
Koichi Hiraoka works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1980–1984) and is attested as a visiting professor at Shuchiin University in 2026.

Koichi Hokazono is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University. He held positions at Kagoshima International University (attested 1991–2000) and Kyushu University (attested 1995).

Koichi Shinohara specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He served as a professor at McMaster University (~1972–2004) and as a senior lecturer in religious studies at Yale University (~2004–2017).

Koichi Takahashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima and Akira Saito, and held posts there as research assistant, project researcher, and professor (attested 2005–2026).

Koichi Yokoyama worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and traditional teacher Gyōin Hashimoto, and served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University (~1975–2005).
Koin Takada (1924–1998) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1944–1947) and was a disciple of Gyōin Hashimoto (~1937–1978), whom he succeeded in 1967.

Koji Kamioka was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara, lectured at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969), and served at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

Koji Shindo is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He was a part-time lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015) and a graduate student at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026).
